newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - May 21.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - May 21.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Buyers kept a tight rein on purchases but steadily filled in where inventories thinned, Random Lengths said. Through Tuesday, lumber prices retreated at the mill level as many items developed for prompt shipment. Monday's holiday in Canada and upcoming Memorial Day in U.S. quieted trading.
Trends in panels were mixed, with OSB a bit stronger, Fir flat and Southern Pine vulnerable. Most traders welcomed the Federal Reserve's decision Tuesday not to raise interest rates.

Western S-P-F prices were mostly unchanged in sluggish trade. The Victoria Day holiday in Canada on Monday had many traders starting their week Tuesday. Reports of steady sales at the distribution level encouraged some producers to approach the market with stiff prices. Std&Btr 2x4 was occasionally seen a few dollars below $380, though quotes ranged up to $390. Sales were anemic; a few buyers reported success countering quotes of $330-335 by $10-20, the lumber reporting agency said.

Eastern S-P-F markets were slow after the Canadian holiday. Most retailers reported steady sales but, with prices softening, they replaced with small-volume mixed loads. Wholesalers still took modest short positions. Narrows of #1-2 were vulnerable.
Canadian shipments as of May 10 were running at 12.8 percent of the annual April/March quota, Random Lengths said.
Southern Pine traded off $5-10 on quick loads but two-week wood had to bne discounted as much as $15-20 to attract buyers. Inquiry picked up Tuesday but most calls were routine checking.
Inland sales of dimension and studs were lethrgic. Most prices softened, with weakness most notable in the wides.
Inland Hem-Fir, #2&Btr 2x10 (Spokane) was available at some mills below $530, while 2x12 was the weaker item in California. Studs sold quietly while board prices were firm to stronger.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir sales were slow and most prices unchanged. Customers did more checking Tuesday but producers often had to concede on prices or tallies to get orders. Fir #2&Btr 2x10 and 2x12, off $5, were sold as low as $550. Hem-Fir prices held across the board, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine plywood sales were slow as buyers sensed weakness and waited for lower prices before stepping in to replenish inventories. Most mills resisted deep cuts, leaving prices flat to slightly lower. Wholesalers took modest short positions in anticipation of month-end discounts, it said.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment sales were dull in early trading. But order files extending into the weeks of May 26 and June 2 left prices flat. The 3/8-inch and 1/2-inch 4-ply sold below printed levels in spots. Fir sanded prices were flat but some hardwood-faced panels were discounted.

OSB prices were firm to higher although the pace of trading cooled a notch. Most mills were booked into next week or the week of June 2. Two-tiered pricing developed as secondaries undercut mill quotes, Random Lengths said.
